result.title: Fewer than a third of the world’s CEOs are women, UN data shows
result.description:
Women hold just 31% of #management positions worldwide, according to a new survey by the @ILO.

This is despite the fact that businesses led by a female #CEO are 6% more likely to report higher profits - while those with a female chair are 18% more likely.

The Global Gender Gap Report 2026 charts a significant ‘drop to the top’: while 46% of entry-level workers are #women, just 23% of those in the C-suite are women.

Tap the link in our bio to read the full report.

result.title: This new glue could make batteries greener
result.description:
Recycling lithium batteries could one day be as simple as soaking them in water.

Researchers at UC San Diego have developed a new water-soluble glue that could make #lithium batteries easier to recycle - without compromising performance.

Their invention could help cut the energy and emissions involved in #battery production, contributing toward a circular battery supply chain. Here’s how it works.

result.title: MRI Scanner Comes to Patients & 5 New Technologies for Planetary Health | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:14 - This helium-free MRI machine can be brought to patients:
Standard MRI scanners are expensive, hard to transport, and rely on a scarce and finite resource. This new micro-cooled MRI scanner uses less than 0.5% as much helium, and is designed specifically to be loaded onto a truck and delivered to patients in remote places. Here, Roy Jakobs, CEO of Philips, explains how it works. 

02:40 - Surviving the Mexico City earthquake as a teen shaped this architect’s approach to urban planning:
Antonio Gomez Palacio, Partner and Chair of design practice DIALOG, was a teenager when a huge earthquake struck Mexico City in 1985. He saw first-hand the scale of destruction, and watched as the city rebuilt itself in the years that followed. It has informed the way he understands and responds to the biggest challenges facing #cities and their inhabitants today: affordability, social inequality and #climate change.

06:05 - Why is clean energy taking so long? Industry experts explain:
The energy transition began three decades ago - and yet renewables still provide just a third of global electricity and 14% of the primary energy supply. So what’s the hold-up? We asked Bruce Douglas of the Global Renewables Alliance, Chao Zhang of Ming Yang Smart Energy Group, Georgios Stassis of PPC and Gyanesh Chaudhary of Vikram Solar.

09:31 - 5 new technologies that could save the planet:
From easy-build nuclear reactors to super-efficient #solar cells, here are 5 emerging technologies that could accelerate the energy transition. You can see all 10 innovations profiled in a new World Economic Forum report, introduced by planetary health scientist Johan Rockström.

result.title: Energy and resource systems are changing. Here’s what that means for skills
result.description:
As energy and resource systems face rising pressures, workforces need a new set of capabilities, known as transition skills.  

Energy and resource transition skills look different across sectors: for an #energy worker, they could mean improving the efficiency and reliability of a system, while for a farmer, they could mean improving soil health through regenerative practices.
